title: Session identifier among ordinary cookies in a Cookie header
summary: A synthetic Cookie request header with a preference cookie, a session-identifier cookie whose name states its role, and a locale cookie.
rationale: Only the session-identifier value is a credential; the cookie name, the separators and the neighbouring ordinary cookies are not. A span that covers the whole header over-covers ordinary cookies, and one that stops at the first separator or inside the nonce under-covers. The extent is the value of the identified cookie, with the name as the context marker.

expectation.rationale: Flag the value of the session-identifier cookie, between its equals sign and the next separator. RFC 6265 says a session identifier in a cookie is a nonce that lets a holder interact with the server; the role here comes from the fixture's own cookie name, since the standard assigns no name meaning (see the unresolved name-classification case).

sources.supports: servers commonly store a nonce (or "session identifier") in a cookie; the nonce is useful only for interacting with the server
